sentences.text: Inkayacu was among the largest fossil penguins, measuring 1.5 meters long and weighing between 54.6 and 59.4 kilograms.
Analysis of melanosomes in Inkayacu feathers indicates the bird had gray or reddish-brown plumage.
The fossil skeleton of Inkayacu includes fossilized feathers, representing the first known feathers preserved in any penguin.
Fossils of Inkayacu were first found in 2008 on the Pacific coast of Ica, Peru.
The skeleton was uncovered from the Otuma Formation in the Paracas National Reserve by an expedition led by Rodolfo Salas and studied by a team led by Julia Clarke.
The genus name Inkayacu translates to "Water Emperor" or "king of the water" from Quechua words.
The species name paracasensis refers to the Paracas region where the fossils were discovered.
Inkayacu's paddle-like limbs enabled an aquatic lifestyle.
Inkayacu is classified as a genus of extinct penguins.
The only species within the genus Inkayacu is I. paracasensis.
The genus Inkayacu was described by Clarke et al. in 2010.
Inkayacu inhabited the seas of Peru during the Late Eocene.
Inkayacu lived between 37.71 and 33.9 million years ago during the Priabonian stage.
It is debated whether modern penguin melanosomes provide an underwater advantage, as their white undersides lack melanin rigidity.
